text:
Joel Hofer was the story in St. Louis, and the final score barely shows it. The Blues goalie stopped 31 of 32 shots, and by our numbers Boston's chances should have produced about 2.65 goals, so he saved roughly 1.65 more than an average goalie would have. Hofer was drafted 107th overall in 2018 and spent 2020-21 splitting time in the AHL with Utica, where he posted a .898 save percentage. On this night he looked like the best player on the ice.

That is also why the 4-1 result flatters St. Louis. Boston outshot the Blues 32 to 18 and attempted 66 shots to 38. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, were close (2.65 for BOS, 2.47 for STL), and our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, leaned slightly toward Boston at 53 percent. James Hagens opened the scoring with a tip-in at 5:28 of the first, a 7 percent chance. Mason McTavish had the best look of the night, a 44 percent chance in the first period that Jeremy Swayman stopped.

St. Louis cashed in where it counted. Jimmy Snuggerud tied it on the power play late in the first, Philip Broberg and Robert Thomas scored in the second, and Jake Neighbours added a power-play goal in the third. The Blues went 2 for 3 with the man advantage while Boston went 0 for 2. Thomas and Broberg each had a goal and two assists, and Thomas, a 20th overall pick in 2017, took first star. We have no standings or streaks to report, but Boston will wonder how 32 shots produced a single goal, and St. Louis will take a win it needed its goalie to earn.
